definitions.explanation: The act of a ship leaving a harbor or port. Used in maritime, travel, and news contexts.

examples.japanese: {船|ふね}が{出港|しゅっこう}した。
{台風|たいふう}の{影響|えいきょう}で{出港|しゅっこう}が{延期|えんき}された。
examples.english: The departure was postponed due to the typhoon.

examples.japanese: フェリーは{毎朝|まいあさ}8{時|じ}に{横浜港|よこはまこう}を{出港|しゅっこう}する。
examples.english: The ferry departs from Yokohama Port every morning at 8 o'clock.

notes:
The act of a ship leaving port. Used as both a noun and a する verb.

FORMS:
{出|しゅつ} (exit/leave) + {港|こう} (port/harbor)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出港|しゅっこう}する: to depart from port
- {出港|しゅっこう}{時刻|じこく}: departure time
- {出港|しゅっこう}{手続|てつづ}き: departure procedures
- {出港|しゅっこう}を{見送|みおく}る: to see a ship off

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {入港|にゅうこう}: entering port (opposite)
- {出航|しゅっこう}: setting sail (same reading, broader — can include aircraft or general departure)

Note the homophone {出航|しゅっこう}: {出港|しゅっこう} specifically means leaving a port, while {出航|しゅっこう} means beginning a voyage and can apply more broadly.
